\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پری} (pari)}{پری (pari)}]{\fa{پری} (pari) — a fairy, a peri}

\label{lesson:FA-C348-pari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a dragon, then the Persian for a demon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پری}}
\textbf{\fa{پری}} (\emph{pari}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fairy, a peri\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{قصه} \fa{یک} \fa{پری} \fa{زیبا} \fa{به} \fa{پسر} \fa{کمک} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar qesse yek pari-ye zibâ be pesar komak kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the tale a beautiful fairy helped the boy.
\end{quote}

Also a girl's name. \emph{Pari-ru} \textquotedblleft{}fairy-faced\textquotedblright{}, very beautiful.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pari} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \emph{parīg}, a female spirit that was once feared as a witch and later became the lovely fairy of poetry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pari}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pari}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a dragon, then the Persian for a demon, then say \emph{pari} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جادو} (jâdu)}{جادو (jâdu)}]{\fa{جادو} (jâdu) — magic, a spell}

\label{lesson:FA-C348-jadu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a demon, then the Persian for a fairy.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جادو}}
\textbf{\fa{جادو}} (\emph{jâdu}) — \textquotedblleft{}magic, a spell\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{با} \fa{جادو} \fa{در} \fa{باز} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâ jâdu dar bâz shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The door opened by magic.
\end{quote}

\emph{Jâdui} \textquotedblleft{}magic, magical\textquotedblright{}: \emph{farsh-e jâdui} \textquotedblleft{}a magic carpet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jâdu} is a native Persian word; EtymDB lists it without a parent.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جادوگر} (jâdugar)}{جادوگر (jâdugar)}]{\fa{جادوگر} (jâdugar) — a witch, a wizard}

\label{lesson:FA-C348-jadugar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fairy, then the Persian for magic.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جادوگر}}
\textbf{\fa{جادوگر}} (\emph{jâdugar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a witch, a wizard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جادوگر} \fa{شاهزاده} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{سنگ} \fa{تبدیل} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jâdugar shâhzâde râ be sang tabdil kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The witch turned the prince into stone.
\end{quote}

\emph{jâdu} \textquotedblleft{}magic\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-gar} \textquotedblleft{}one who does\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jâdugar} is built from Persian \emph{jâdu} \textquotedblleft{}magic\textquotedblright{}, a native word, with the suffix \emph{-gar} \textquotedblleft{}one who does\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرنوشت} (sarnevesht)}{سرنوشت (sarnevesht)}]{\fa{سرنوشت} (sarnevesht) — fate, destiny}

\label{lesson:FA-C348-sarnevesht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a witch, then the Persian for a treasure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرنوشت}}
\textbf{\fa{سرنوشت}} (\emph{sarnevesht}) — \textquotedblleft{}fate, destiny\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سرنوشت} \fa{آنها} \fa{را} \fa{دوباره} \fa{به} \fa{هم} \fa{رساند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sarnevesht ânhâ râ dobâre be ham resând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Fate brought them together again.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}what is written on the head\textquotedblright{}: \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} + \emph{nevesht} \textquotedblleft{}writing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarnevesht} joins \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} and \emph{nevesht}, the past stem of \emph{neveshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB glosses it \textquotedblleft{}destiny, fate\textquotedblright{}. Both parts are native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
